Bungie is seeking a Senior Systems Engineer with a focus on End User Experience (EUX) and Endpoint Engineering to join our Studio IT team. This role will help design, build, and improve the technology experience used by Bungie employees every day, with a focus on secure, reliable, and scalable endpoint platforms and services.

Are you passionate about making technology easier and more dependable for the people using it? Do you enjoy solving complex endpoint problems, automating repetitive work, and improving how devices and applications are deployed and managed? Can you balance security, usability, and operational needs without creating unnecessary friction for our users? Then come help Bungie IT Engineering support the teams creating our world-class games.

As a Senior Systems Engineer at Bungie, you will architect, implement, and support endpoint platforms, device management, application delivery, and supporting infrastructure across Bungie’s environment. You’ll work with a team of experienced IT engineers and partner closely with Studio IT Support, Information Security, infrastructure teams, application owners, and development teams to continuously improve the technology experience for our users.

This role is expected to take technical ownership of EUX platforms and services, identify recurring pain points, and build solutions that reduce friction for both users and support teams. You will help establish standards, automate common workflows, and ensure endpoint services can scale with the changing needs of game development.

Successful candidates will have strong experience engineering and supporting enterprise endpoint environments, be comfortable owning complex technical problems, and be able to turn user and business needs into practical technical solutions.   • Architect, implement, and maintain endpoint management platforms and services supporting Bungie employees and development teams

  • Mentor engineers and provide technical guidance and training to Studio IT Support and other technical teams

Required Skills

  • Strong experience engineering and operating endpoint management solutions in a large enterprise environment
  • Experience with Microsoft Intune, Ivanti and other modern endpoint management technologies
  • Strong knowledge of Windows endpoint architecture, configuration, deployment, troubleshooting, and lifecycle management
  • Experience managing macOS endpoints using enterprise device-management technologies
  • Experience with automated device provisioning technologies such as Windows Autopilot, Apple Automated Device Enrollment, or comparable solutions
  • Experience with enterprise software packaging, deployment, patching, and application lifecycle management
  • Experience designing and enforcing endpoint configuration and compliance policies
  • Experience automating administrative and endpoint workflows using PowerShell, Python, APIs, or comparable technologies
  • Experience troubleshooting complex endpoint issues across operating systems, applications, identity, networking, and security layers
  • Understanding of Active Directory and Microsoft Entra ID as they relate to endpoint authentication, device identity, policy, and access
  • Understanding of endpoint security technologies and concepts including EDR, disk encryption, local privilege management, certificates, and device compliance
  • Experience independently leading complex technical projects involving multiple teams and stakeholders
  • Demonstrated ability to partner with support organizations and turn recurring operational issues into engineering improvements
  • Ability to evaluate technical decisions from both an engineering and end-user perspective
  • Ability to mentor other engineers and help establish technical standards and best practices
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent

Nice-to-Have Skills

  • Experience with Windows Autopilot and modern Windows provisioning

jobs.excerpt: About EngineEngine is the AI-native platform for intelligent travel.
jobs.description:
About Engine

Engine is the AI-native platform for intelligent travel. For a decade, Engine has built the proprietary technology and supply behind modern business travel, serving over 40,000 customers and nearly 2 million travelers, along with leading travel and AI companies that build on Engine's infrastructure. One system powers business travel, group travel, human agents, and AI agents.

That work has earned recognition as one of Fast Company's Best Workplaces for Innovators (2025), TravelTech's Reservation Platform of the Year (2026), and one of Built In's Best Places to Work (2020–2026).

We're looking for bold, ambitious people to help redefine how businesses manage and experience travel. Working here, you can expect exponential growth, an ambitious pace, full ownership, and high-caliber colleagues who push you to do the best work of your career. Every hire raises the bar.

Come outpace the ordinary and build the future of travel with us.

About the Role

Engine's Partner Growth team partners with a growing ecosystem of associations, fintech platforms, and distribution partners to bring Engine's free-to-use travel product to their members and customers. As Senior Partner Growth Manager, you will own the full lifecycle of Engine's most important channel relationships, from onboarding and enablement through deep performance optimization, driving revenue share growth across a portfolio that spans industries and partner types: associations, fintech and corporate spending platforms, marketplaces, and other distribution partners.

This is not a reactive account management role. You will function as a channel expert inside Engine's Partner Growth org, building the playbooks, relationships, and commercial frameworks that allow Engine to scale distribution through partners without sacrificing traveler experience or commercial performance. You'll sit at the intersection of partner acquisition and strategic account management, and you'll be expected to lead both internally and externally.

Why This Role Exists

Engine's channel partner network is entering a new phase of maturity. As the partner ecosystem grows and our largest relationships deepen, we need a dedicated owner who can enable partners to effectively position and distribute Engine to their audiences, and who understands the commercial levers that drive revenue share performance at scale. This hire is a critical seat on the channel team and is expected to immediately pick up a book of active relationships and drive them forward with minimal ramp time.

What You'll Own

Channel Partner Growth & Performance

  • Own end-to-end partner growth for a portfolio of channel partners spanning a range of industries, partner models, and scales
  • Drive GBV growth within existing channel partnerships through proactive commercial reviews, optimization initiatives, and joint go-to-market planning
  • Monitor partner health across production metrics, rate quality, and engagement, flagging risks and surfacing opportunities before they become problems
  • Ensure every partner in your portfolio has a regular cadence of meaningful touchpoints (no partner goes 60+ days without one), catching adoption or engagement gaps before they become churn risks
  • Lead QBRs and executive business reviews for strategic partners and structured health check-ins for the broader portfolio, translating data into forward-looking strategy rather than backward-looking reporting
  • Manage the commercial and contractual dimensions of partner relationships, including pricing discussions, tier reviews, and renewal negotiations
  • Serve as the first line of escalation for partner issues, coordinating internally with supply, product, and engineering to drive resolution
  • Own partner tier progression: actively move partners from Bronze toward Gold/Platinum status by unlocking the right milestones
  • Build multi-threaded relationships inside each partner across commercial, product, marketing, and operational contacts, so Engine's position doesn't depend on a single champion
  • Develop deep institutional knowledge of each partner's business model, product roadmap, and internal champions

Channel Ecosystem Development

  • Engage at contract signature to understand each partner's goals, stakeholders, and definition of success, then own the transition from the Partner Acquisition team to ongoing partner growth
  • Build and maintain channel-specific playbooks, onboarding frameworks, and partner enablement materials
  • Be the voice of the live partner base in internal product and roadmap discussions, translating partner needs into structured feature requests
  • Partner with the VP of Partner Growth to define the channel partner strategy and inform partner prioritization decisions
  • Identify expansion opportunities within existing partner footprints: new use cases, geographies, user segments, or product lines
  • Partner with Sales and Marketing to align channel activity to co-sell motions and joint go-to-market initiatives
  • Contribute to the buildout of scalable channel infrastructure: tier frameworks, health scoring, comp model inputs, and reporting tooling

Who You Are

You're the kind of person who...

  • Has operated in a channel, distribution, or platform partnerships role and understands what it takes to make indirect revenue models work
  • Thrives in the post-sale: you enjoy turning a signed partnership into a performing one and don't need the thrill of the new-logo chase to stay motivated. Proactive, not reactive.
  • Builds trust with external partners quickly. You're commercially fluent, technically credible, and curious about how their business works
  • Owns outcomes, not activities. You track GBV, conversion rates, and partner health, and you know what levers to pull when numbers move in the wrong direction
  • Is comfortable managing a diverse portfolio, able to prioritize across partners of different sizes, industries, and models without letting anything fall through the cracks; you have systems, not just good intentions
  • Is comfortable in ambiguity and can structure your own work without constant direction
  • Brings a point of view to the table in internal discussions. You advocate for your partners while holding Engine's commercial interests clearly in mind
  • Has a high bar for communication: written, verbal, and visual. You can synthesize a complex partner situation into a clear executive update

Experience & Qualifications

Required

  • 5+ years in partner growth, partner success, strategic account management, or channel partnerships, ideally in travel tech, fintech, SaaS, or a distribution-heavy business
  • Demonstrated track record managing complex, high-value B2B relationships with measurable GBV or revenue outcomes
  • Experience managing partners across more than one industry or partner type (e.g., associations, fintech/corporate card, marketplaces, distribution platforms) is a strong differentiator
  • Commercial acumen: comfortable with pricing negotiations, contract terms, and tier-based incentive structures
  • Strong data orientation: you use metrics to tell stories and drive decisions, and you're comfortable building your own analyses in Excel/Google Sheets
  • Experience translating partner needs into internal product or engineering requests, with the credibility to advocate in cross-functional forums

Preferred

  • Experience running co-marketing or partner enablement programs (webinars, member communications, sales-team training, or embedded placements) that measurably lifted partner-sourced volume
  • Hands-on experience with partner commercial contracts, including structuring, negotiating, and renewing agreements with revenue-share terms, exclusivity, SLAs, and amendments, and partnering with Legal and Finance to get them across the line
  • Experience building partnerships playbooks, onboarding frameworks, or health scoring models, and familiarity with partner ecosystem tools like Crossbeam
  • Exposure to comp plan design or partner incentive structures (SPIFs, tier bonuses, go-live milestones)

Compensation & Structure

Role context

  • Compensation is structured as a base + variable model
  • This role sits within the Partner Growth team, reporting to the VP of Partner Growth
  • Travel required for partner QBRs, industry events, and periodic on-sites (~20%)

Engine is an equal opportunity employer committed to building a diverse and inclusive team.

Applications for this role will be accepted through December 22nd, 2026, or until the role is filled. We encourage you to apply early, as we may begin reviewing applications before the deadline.

OTE Compensation
In addition to a competitive base salary, our listed compensation range includes the estimated variable target. Your OTE (on-target earnings) are based on several factors including your experience, expertise, and location. In addition, all roles receive equity. Your recruiter will share your complete compensation package as you move through the process.

Total OTE Range (Base Salary + Variable)
$160,000—$215,000 USD

The Engine Edge: Perks & Compensation
We believe in rewarding great work with great benefits:

  • Compensation: Competitive base pay tied to role and experience, with equity for all employees. Some roles are also eligible for bonuses or commissions.
  • Benefits: Check out our full list at
  • Environments for Success: Different roles have different needs in terms of the environments that drive success which is why we have a hybrid-hub model. Whether you are in one of our amazing offices or fully remote, we'll make sure you have what you need to succeed.

Perks and benefits may vary based on employment type, location, and more

jobs.description:
Greenhouse is the first Orchestrated Hiring Ecosystem: a single place that brings the right person and the right role together at the right time. Our mission is to make hiring work for everyone – so we go to great lengths to hire great people because we believe that they’re the foundation of our success. At Greenhouse, you’ll join a team that collaborates purposefully, fosters inclusivity, and communicates with transparency and accountability so we can achieve our mission.

Join us to do the best work of your career, solving meaningful problems with remarkable teams.

Greenhouse is looking for a Senior Revenue Systems Specialist to join our team!

Revenue Systems owns the go-to-market technology stack at Greenhouse, from first outreach through renewal. As a Senior Revenue Systems Specialist, you’ll own systems work across both pre-sale and post-sale: Salesforce, our sales system of record, and the platforms our Customer Success and Customer Marketing teams work from every day, currently Gainsight and Accord. Breadth is a key aspect of this role, and you’ll have real latitude to shape where the stack goes next.

Who will love this job

  • A systems generalist - you enjoy working across a stack rather than being confined to one corner of it, and you’re comfortable moving to where the work is
  • A solutions-orientedpartner - you can hear what the business is trying to accomplish and turn it into something that works, and you stay with a problem until the desired outcome is achieved
  • A curious builder - you want to understand why a process exists before you automate it, and you’re comfortable saying when something doesn’t seem to make sense, including to the people asking for it
  • An owner - you take a project from first conversation through rollout and adoption without needing it project-managed for you
  • An AI-fluent operator - you already use tools like Claude, Glean, or ChatGPT in your day to day, and you’re interested in what they can do inside a revenue stack

What you’ll do

  • Own and build solutions in Salesforce, including data model design, declarative automation, validation, permissions, page layouts, and reporting, taking projects from scoping and intake through rollout, adoption, and documentation
  • Administer our post-sale platforms, including Gainsight and Accord, alongside our Customer Success Operations team, covering the rules engine, journey and email programs, surveys including NPS, and the workflows behind customer health scoring, CSM assignment, and account transfers
  • Own integrations between Salesforce, Gainsight, and the rest of the stack, standing up new ones independently and eliminating the recurring failures that come with the existing ones
  • Partner with Sales, Customer Success, and Customer Marketing on their requests, working out whether the fix belongs in a system or somewhere else, and seeing it through to a working solution either way
  • Lead platform migration and consolidation work as our tech stack changes, from evaluation and vendor assessment through data movement, cutover, and adoption
  • Hold a point of view on where the stack should go, surfacing the opportunities and the risks in our implementation rather than waiting to be asked
  • Document what you build, and bring request volume down over time through automation and self-service
  • Additional projects and responsibilities as business needs require

You should have

  • Several years in revenue operations, customer success operations, business systems, or platform administration.
  • B2B SaaS experience.
  • Deep hands-on Salesforce administration experience: data model design, declarative automation, permissions and sharing, reporting, and the judgment to know when not to build. You should be comfortable making medium to large changes to a production org and reasoning about the performance and scale implications of your configuration choices.
  • Hands-on ownership of Gainsight or a comparable post-sale platform (e.g., Totango, ChurnZero, Planhat), with enough depth to configure independently and to hold a credible view on whether the platform is serving the business.
  • Experience standing up integrations without support, and a record of eliminating recurring failures rather than only resolving them.
  • Experience owning a platform migration or consolidation end to end, including the data movement.
  • A track record of taking a problem from the first report through to a working solution.
  • Comfort operating as the most knowledgeable person in the room on a platform, and the instinct to bring others along rather than becoming the only one who can do the work.
  • Clear writing. A real part of this job is explaining to a non-technical stakeholder what you built and how to use it, or what went wrong and what you did about it.
  • Experience across more than one post-sale platform is a plus. So is exposure to Salesforce CPQ, enrichment tooling like Clay, or building with MCP and agentic tooling against enterprise systems.
  • Your own unique talents! Your background has given you a unique perspective and set of transferable skills that aren’t always in alignment with a given role, but those are qualities we value at Greenhouse. If you don’t meet 100% of the qualifications outlined above, we still strongly encourage you to apply.

Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis.

If you are based in California, we encourage you to read this important information for California residents linkedhere.

The national pay range for this role is $88,100.00 - $127,700.00. Individual compensation will be commensurate with the candidate's experience and qualifications. Certain roles may be eligible for additional compensation, including stock option awards, bonuses, and merit increases. Additionally, certain roles have the opportunity to receive sales commissions that are based on the terms of the sales commission plan applicable to the role.

Greenhouse provides a variety of benefits to employees, including medical, dental, and vision insurance, basic life insurance, mental health resources, financial wellness benefits, and a fully paid parental leave program. For US-based employees, we offer short-term and long-term disability coverage, a 401(k) plan and company match. U.S. based employees also receive, per calendar year, up to 14 scheduled paid holidays and up to 80 hours of paid sick leave. Non-exempt employees accrue up to 20-25 days of paid vacation time annually, depending on tenure, and exempt employees have flexible paid time off (PTO).

The anticipated closing date for this role is Friday, November 13, 2026.

Who we are

At Greenhouse, we live by our mission through using our own product to help us hire the right person for the job, every time. We’re committed to designing and responsibly using AI tools to transform how we work while keeping people at the center. We are a remote-first company and have shared office spaces in New York City and Ireland, and optional co-working spaces that give us flexibility to do our best work anywhere. We take an active role in our growth through a performance review program that’s committed to providing actionable feedback, and a bonus structure that rewards great performance. We believe that bringing together a variety of perspectives makes us a stronger company – and we nurture leaders who create an inclusive culture and invest into employee resource groups that celebrate our differences and life experiences. We’re proud to have built an award-winning culture that’s been recognized as Fortune’s Best Places to Work and Inc.’s Best Workplaces multiple years in a row.

–

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, sexual orientation, or gender identity), national origin, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable local laws, regulations and ordinances. If you need assistance and/or a reasonable accommodation during the application process, reach out to .

jobs.title: Spring 2027 Graduate Intern, Affiliate Support and Nationwide Initiatives - Orga
jobs.excerpt: The ACLU seeks a Graduate Intern for theirAffiliate Support and Nationwide Initiatives Department's (ASNI) Organizational Management, Equity & Inclusion (OMEI) Team of the National ACLU Office in Washington D.
jobs.description:
The ACLU seeks a Graduate Intern for theirAffiliate Support and Nationwide Initiatives Department's (ASNI) Organizational Management, Equity & Inclusion (OMEI) Team of the National ACLU Office in Washington D.C. This internship is remote and can be full-time or part-time.

Qualifying applicants must currently be matriculated Graduate students and must be based in the U.S. for the entire duration of the internship.

The Team:

The ASNI department builds state capacity and strengthens the connections between the ACLU and its network of 54 state affiliates and their 1,500 staff members across the country. The affiliates’ work constitutes an unparalleled bulwark defending and advancing our civil liberties and civil rights. ASNI staff lead efforts to build program, build organizations, and drive resources to key battles across the country, positioning the nationwide organization for future challenges. The Organizational Management, Equity & Inclusion (OMEI) team is a crucial partner to ACLU affiliates and other leaders in change management, leadership development and organization capacity-building.

Our team (OMEI) strengthens affiliates’ organizational health and impact by providing training, coaching, resources, and learning communities that advance strategic and financial management, governance, leadership, and EDIB-centered culture—while helping affiliates effectively leverage multi-year investments to build long-term capacity and belonging.

What You’ll Do:

The intern will be responsible for collaborating with the OMEI team to ensure that the needs of the affiliate staff are met through learning programs, tools, and resources.

This internship supports the following Focus Areas:  Affiliate Organizational Management, Equity, and Inclusion (OMEI)/Affiliate Equity, Diversity, Inclusion, and Belonging (EDIB) Trainings/departmental goals, "Affiliate Equity Pipeline" (Recruitment and Talent Attraction), Southern Legal Internship Program (SLIP). In this internship you will engage in strategic discussions on a nationwide scale, contributing to our commitment to fostering equity, diversity, inclusion, and belonging. You will research and share cutting-edge learnings to support a culture of learning and growth in the realm of Organizational Management, Equity, and Inclusion (OMEI)

Your Day to Day

  • Resource Creation and Management: Create, edit, organize and maintain resources for effective communication of OMEI/SLIP programs and tools. Maintain and update content on "the HUB," our intranet platform. Help analyze data related to Hub usage and Sharedrive file organization.
  • Administrative Support: Assist in coordinating learning calls and webinars, support virtual workshops administration. Support administrative tasks, such as taking notes for and assisting with the coordination of meetings related to working groups, learning communities, and other initiatives.
  • Communication: Draft preliminary language for deliverables, such as internal communications, brief summaries, and PowerPoint presentations, for different audiences. Written correspondence to stakeholders across the nationwide organization.
  • Virtual Meeting Involvement: Attend critical meetings with ACLU affiliate staff and board members, Draft follow-up summaries and communications, documenting key learnings. track next steps.
  • Data Analysis and Reporting: Identify and synthesis relevant data Excel and PowerPoint reports, analyze and report on priority programming and learning community effectiveness, support survey data collection and analysis of results.

What You’ll Bring:

  • Graduate student in related field
  • Word, PowerPoint and Excel proficiency
  • Interest in organizational management, equity, inclusion, and belonging
  • Experience with project management and building resources
  • Ability to take initiative, think creatively, contribute innovative ideas, problem solve, work well under pressure, and take ownership of projects and assignments
  • Experience assisting with administrative tasks in an office setting, preferably a nonprofit
  • A commitment to civil liberties, civil rights, and social justice 

Future ACLU-ers Will:

  • Be committed to advancing the mission of the ACLU
  • Center and embed the principles of equity, inclusion and belonging in their work by demonstrating commitment to diversity with an approach that respects and values multiple perspectives
  • Be committed to work collaboratively and respectfully toward resolving obstacles and conflict

Internship Logistics:

  • Location: Our internship program offers a limited number of remote or hybrid intern positions. This internship can be full-time or part-time and remote from our Washington D.C. office.
  • Time Commitment: Full-time (35 hrs/week) or Part-time (10,15 or 20hrs/wk)
  • Internship Duration: Full-time internships span 10 consecutive weeks and Part-time internships span 12 consecutive weeks. This internship has a start date of: Jan. 11th or Jan. 25th, 2027
  • Stipend: A stipend is available for students who are lawfully authorized to work. Arrangements can be made with educational institutions for work/study or course credit.
    • Below is the stipend rate:
      • $24/hr for graduate and law students or equivalent experience

Priority Application Deadline: Friday, November 13, 2026.

While there is a priority deadline, our project is committed to reviewing all applications on a rolling basis until the closing of posting.

Why the ACLU:

For over 100 years, the ACLU has worked to defend and preserve the individual rights and liberties guaranteed by the Constitution and laws of the United States. Whether it’s ending mass incarceration, achieving full equality for the LGBTQ+ community, establishing new privacy protections for our digital age, or preserving the right to vote or the right to have an abortion, the ACLU takes up the toughest civil liberties cases and issues to defend all people.

Our Commitment to Accessibility, Equity, Diversity and Inclusion
Accessibility, equity, diversity, and inclusion are core values of the ACLU and central to our work to advance liberty, equality, and justice for all. For us diversity, equity and inclusion are not just check-the-box activities, but a chance for us to make long-term meaningful change. We are a community committed to learning and growth, humility and grace, transparency, and accountability. We believe in a collective responsibility to create a culture of belonging for all people within our organization – one that respects and embraces difference; treats everyone equitably; and empowers our colleagues to do the best work possible. We are as committed to anti-oppression and anti-racism internally as we are externally. Because whether we’re in the courts or in the office, we believe ‘We the People’ means all of us. 

With this commitment in mind, we strongly encourage applications from all qualified individuals without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, national origin, marital status, citizenship, disability, veteran status and record of arrest or conviction, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. 

To maintain the integrity of our assessment process, please refrain from using AI-powered chatbots, search engines, or real-time assistance tools to generate your CV, cover letter or writing sample (if required). We want to better understand your individual skills and thought processes. If you require AI tools or other assistive technology as a reasonable accommodation due to a disability, please complete the Accommodation Request Form so that we can support an accessible and equitable experience.

If you are selected for an interview, you will receive additional information regarding how to request an accommodation for the interview process.

In order to be considered for this position, all candidates must formally submit an application. The ACLU does not accept unsolicited calls or emails from candidates regarding their application status.

jobs.title: Enterprise Sales Executive, AI Solutions
jobs.excerpt: About ToptalToptal is a global network of top talent in business, design, and technology that enables companies to scale their teams, on-demand.
jobs.description:
About Toptal

Toptal is a global network of top talent in business, design, and technology that enables companies to scale their teams, on-demand. With $200+ million in annual revenue and team members based around the globe, Toptal is the world’s largest fully remote workforce.

We take the best elements of virtual teams and combine them with a support structure that encourages innovation, social interaction, and fun. We see no borders, move at a fast pace, and are never afraid to break the mold.

Job Summary:

As an Enterprise Sales Executive at Toptal, you will be a key driver of growth within our AI Solutions business. In this role, you will identify, develop, and close opportunities with enterprise clients by helping them solve complex business challenges through forward-deployed AI solutions, AI software and platforms, AI services, and AI-enabled transformation.

You will develop tailored solutions that help clients move from AI strategy and experimentation into production, combining Toptal’s capabilities across AI Strategy & Transformation, Agentic Solutions, Data Services, AI Platforms, Industry Solutions, Joint Partner Solutions, and Managed Services to achieve measurable business outcomes.

This role is designed for true hunters who thrive in a high-performance, client-facing environment. It is ideal for individuals who have successfully sold enterprise AI solutions and are passionate about building a book of business from the ground up, forging executive relationships, and creating long-term client value. Success in this role is measured by your ability to convert new enterprise relationships into durable revenue and establish Toptal as a core AI services provider embedded in your clients’ most critical initiatives.

Enterprise AI has shifted rapidly from experimentation to execution. Companies are investing in models, agents, AI platforms, data infrastructure, and AI-enabled applications, but many are struggling to translate those investments into production systems and measurable business outcomes.

The challenge is no longer simply selecting an AI model or platform. Enterprises must identify the right workflows, connect AI to their proprietary data and knowledge, integrate existing systems, build and deploy agents and applications, establish evaluation and control frameworks, drive adoption, and continuously operate and improve AI in production.

Toptal brings together world-class AI and domain talent, forward-deployed solution delivery, AI platforms and capabilities, strategic technology partners, expert-in-the-loop operations, and managed services to help enterprises move from AI promise to production.

This role exists to convert that market opportunity into new enterprise relationships and position Toptal as a strategic partner for companies deploying AI across their organizations.

This is a remote position with significant client-facing fieldwork across the US. Applicants who reside within commutable distance of a major metropolitan area are strongly preferred. We do not offer visa sponsorship or assistance. Resumes and communication must be submitted in English.

Responsibilities:

*The following information is intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed. It is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, or required skills.

You will be responsible for building a targeted portfolio of accounts via identifying, prioritizing, and developing your own book of business rather than inheriting an existing one. Once you have signed net new customers, you will partner with Client Partners to deepen and expand those strategic relationships over time.

Net new accounts may begin with a specific AI initiative, workflow, platform implementation, or business problem requiring a disciplined approach to defining the opportunity and matching the right Toptal capabilities to the client’s needs. As relationships mature, accounts become more complex, with deeper engagement across multiple business units, workflows, technology platforms, and senior executive relationships.

These accounts demand a highly consultative, strategic approach that includes navigating cross-functional priorities, understanding the client’s AI and technology environment, aligning solutions to evolving business objectives, and demonstrating credibility at the C-suite level. Success will require the ability to adapt your engagement style to the maturity and complexity of each account while consistently driving measurable client value and long-term growth.

  • Own and build a portfolio of enterprise AI accounts, with direct accountability for new logo acquisition, revenue growth, and client outcomes.
  • Prospect, pitch, negotiate, and close new opportunities in close partnership with our Sales Development Representatives (SDRs), while expanding the relationships you establish.
  • Define and execute account strategy, including opportunity creation, pipeline development, and multi-year growth planning.
  • Lead AI solution development and deal execution in partnership with AI Services leadership, Industry GMs, Practice Leaders, Pursuits, Partnerships, and Delivery teams.
  • Partner with Client Partners to drive coordinated account expansion and maximize total account value as accounts mature.
  • Shape AI solutions that apply Toptal’s capabilities across AI Strategy & Transformation, Agentic Solutions, Data Services, AI Platforms, Industry Solutions, Joint Partner Solutions, and Managed Services to clients’ most important business and operating challenges.
  • Maintain disciplined pipeline and account intelligence to support accurate forecasting and informed decision-making.
  • Lead strategic conversations with prospective and existing clients, while exercising discretion and independent judgment.

In the first week, expect to:

  • Onboard with Toptal and meet your TopPal.
  • Learn the core of Toptal’s model, our value proposition, and our deep capabilities.
  • Familiarize yourself with the tools and resources needed to be successful.
  • Dive into our sales methods, our selling processes, and playbooks.
  • Become familiar with our contracting and legal methodologies, templates, tools, and processes.

In the first month, expect to:

  • Meet key Toptal stakeholders who will support your success and the success of the overall team.
  • Learn about the Toptal AI Go-To-Market Strategy, our key sales plays, solution portfolio, partner ecosystem, and client engagement model.
  • Work with AI Services leadership to establish a portfolio strategy and build account plans.
  • Shadow key calls and client meetings.
  • Begin to meet with clients, leveraging your existing enterprise AI network and relationships, to articulate Toptal’s capabilities and identify where we can help organizations move AI into production.
  • Begin prospecting and actively engaging target accounts within your portfolio.
  • Meet with SDRs, Client Partners, and cross-functional team members to align on joint account strategies.
  • Collaborate with Pursuits and Delivery teams to understand how we design AI engagements.

In the first three months, expect to:

  • Exercise discretion and independent judgment in the negotiation of contracts, work collaboratively with clients, and help them engage with Toptal’s AI capabilities and specialists.
  • Begin shaping AI solutions that resonate with your target accounts, including forward-deployed AI solutions, Outcome Agents, agentic workflows, enterprise data and knowledge solutions, AI platforms, and managed AI services, demonstrating your comfort and ability in working with ambiguity and directly innovating alongside your clients.
  • Establish credibility with client stakeholders through informed, consultative engagement tied to their AI priorities, business workflows, existing technology investments, and desired outcomes.
  • Own your pipeline and forecast with confidence.
  • Develop proposals and close your first set of deals.
  • Actively contribute to team rituals, best practice sharing, and win/loss reviews.

In the first six months, expect to:

  • Have an initial base of active clients while continuing to build your overall portfolio.
  • Expand your buyer network and deepen executive engagement across your accounts.
  • Drive net new opportunities by introducing additional AI capabilities, platforms, solutions, partners, and managed services and displacing incumbent providers.
  • Shape and influence client priorities, aligning Toptal’s AI solutions to critical business objectives and measurable, validated outcomes.
  • Execute against a defined growth plan tied to measurable outcomes.

In the first year, expect to:

  • Have built a list of incredible client accounts, advising them on how to utilize Toptal’s AI capabilities to address their priorities and key business challenges.
  • Establish and expand a strong executive network across your portfolio, building a foundation of advocates and sponsors.
  • Begin to mentor new members of the team, teaching them about Toptal, our AI model, and how to successfully grow their territory.
  • Be recognized for your subject matter expertise in enterprise AI solutions, leveraging your existing network and relationships as well as your proven consultative selling skills to drive meaningful results for your clients and the overall AI Services team.

Qualifications and Job Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree is required.
  • 7-10+ years of experience in enterprise technology, AI software, professional services, or consulting sales, with a strong foundation in enterprise account development and complex solution selling.
  • Direct experience selling enterprise AI solutions is required, ideally including forward-deployed AI solutions, AI software or platforms, AI consulting and professional services, or managed AI services.
  • Extensive experience in consultative customer engagement and selling service-oriented, technology-enabled, or outcome-based solutions to enterprise clients.
  • Demonstrated success building a book of business from the ground up, i.e. self-sourcing, prospecting, and developing new enterprise relationships rather than relying on an inherited portfolio.
  • Proven track record managing a $5M+ annualized gross portfolio and closing $250K-$1M+ complex, multi-phase deals with enterprise clients with $2B+ in annual revenue.
  • Must be comfortable engaging C-level executives on how AI is changing their business, technology environment, operating model, workforce, and competitive landscape.
  • A well-rounded understanding of enterprise AI challenges and trends, including generative AI, agentic AI, AI applications and platforms, enterprise data and knowledge, models, workflow automation, governance, evaluation, controls, and managed AI operations.
  • Ability to have informed discussions about how AI moves from strategy and experimentation into real enterprise workflows and production environments, including the importance of context, data, integration, validation, governance, adoption, and ongoing operations.
  • Experience selling solutions involving leading AI, cloud, data, or enterprise technology platforms, and the ability to work in a platform-flexible environment across client technology ecosystems.
  • Exposure to hybrid talent models, forward-deployed delivery models, or alternative consulting delivery models.
  • Ability to build and execute account plans that lead to consistent portfolio growth and a healthy pipeline.
  • Proven success in collaborative prospecting, running virtual and on-site sales calls, and leading sales pursuits backed by a multidisciplinary team.
  • Experience negotiating complex service agreements with procurement and legal departments within enterprise accounts.
  • Ability to partner effectively across multiple internal teams to shape innovative solutions that drive client success.
  • Willingness and ability to travel to client sites, conferences, and team events (up to 25%).
  • Passion for solving client problems with creativity and urgency.
  • Regular or periodic travel to meet and engage with Toptal clients and customers both inside and outside of your geographic location.
  • Outstanding written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to work in a fast-paced, rapidly growing company and handle a wide variety of challenges, deadlines, and a diverse array of contacts.
  • You must be a world-class individual contributor to thrive at Toptal. You will not be here just to tell other people what to do.

jobs.title: Account Manager, Clio
jobs.excerpt: About UsScorpion is the leading provider of technology and services helping local businesses thrive.
jobs.description:
About Us

Scorpion is the leading provider of technology and services helping local businesses thrive. We do this by helping customers understand local market dynamics, make the most of their marketing, and deliver experiences their customers will love. We offer tools to know what’s going on with marketing, competitors, and customers. We offer a unique blend of AI support and teams of real human people with local expertise committed to customer success. At Scorpion, we are ready to do whatever it takes to help our clients reach their goals. Our technology and personalized tools bring everything together to help local businesses easily understand their unique business, market, and customer needs. We put SEO, Reviews, Advertising, Email Marketing, Chat and Messaging, Social Media, Website, Lead Management, Appointment Scheduling, and more to work for local businesses. We’re a technology-led service with a human touch.

About the Role

Scorpion is looking for a proactive, client-focused Account Manager to support a growing segment of legal clients generated through our partnership with Clio. This is a unique opportunity to help build a new client engagement function from the ground up. You’ll work directly with Scorpion hosting clients who use Clio as their primary case-management platform, helping them activate and get value from the Scorpion–Clio integration, increasing engagement, and identifying opportunities to expand their relationship with Scorpion over time.

Because this is a developing function, you won’t simply step into an established playbook. You’ll help create it. From developing outreach strategies and call scripts to testing new approaches and identifying what drives client engagement, you’ll have the opportunity to influence how Scorpion supports and grows this client segment.

This role is a strong fit for someone who enjoys working with clients, is comfortable with proactive outreach, has an interest in sales and growth, and is energized by building new processes and finding better ways to engage customers.

What your success will look like

  • Drive Client Activation and Adoption Engage newly launched clients to ensure they successfully activate and utilize the Scorpion–Clio integration, identifying and addressing barriers to adoption.
  • Increase Client Engagement Develop proactive outreach strategies that encourage clients to engage with Scorpion and take advantage of the resources and capabilities available to them.
  • Conduct Proactive Client Outreach Connect with clients through phone, email, and other outreach methods. This may include cold or re-engagement outreach to clients who have had limited interaction with Scorpion.
  • Identify Growth Opportunities Use client conversations and available integration data to identify needs and potential opportunities for clients to expand their relationship with Scorpion.
  • Use Data to Inform Outreach Review available integration and client data to understand engagement, identify trends or opportunities, and prioritize client outreach.
  • Build the Playbook Help develop and continuously improve call scripts, email messaging, outreach cadences, engagement strategies, and workflows for this growing client segment.
  • Test and Learn Experiment with different approaches to client engagement, evaluate what works, and use those insights to improve the team's strategy and processes.
  • Collaborate Across Teams Partner with internal teams supporting the Clio partnership, client experience, sales, and other areas of Scorpion to help create a seamless client experience.
  • Support the Clio Partnership As the role develops, there may be opportunities to participate in partnership discussions and quarterly business reviews with Clio and contribute insights about client engagement, adoption, and growth opportunities.

Who you are and what you bring

  • Education
    • Bachelor's degree in Marketing, Advertising, Business, Communications, or a related field—or equivalent practical experience.
  • Experience
    • 2+ years of experience in a client-facing role such as customer success, sales, business development, account coordination, or a related function.
    • Experience conducting proactive client outreach by phone and email.
    • Experience working cross-functionally with multiple teams or stakeholders.
    • Experience in the legal industry, SaaS, digital marketing, or technology integrations is a plus but not required.
  • Skills
    • Strong verbal and written communication skills.
    • Strong relationship-building skills and an interest in client engagement, customer growth, and sales.
    • Ability to use data and client insights to identify trends, priorities, and growth opportunities.
    • Strong problem-solving skills with a willingness to test new approaches and refine strategies based on results.
    • Ability to work independently and create structure in a developing function with limited established processes.
    • Strong organizational skills and follow-through when managing outreach across a large client population.
    • Adaptability and comfort working in an evolving environment where processes and priorities may change.
    • Ability to collaborate effectively across teams and with external partners.
    • Eagerness to learn new platforms, tools, and technologies.
  • Travel
    • The role requires 10% travel within the United States and Canada

Our Scorpion Values

Winning Mindset: When our clients win, we win.
Genuine Care: We only succeed when we are truly invested in our clients and each other.
Unmatched Results: We deliver more than expected–and then some–driving the best results and impacting lives.
Constant Improvement: We believe there is always a better way. We learn we ask “What if?” we build and then do it again.
Unbeatable Teamwork: We come from different backgrounds but have the same vision. We only get there by doing it together, as a team.

Compensation

We acknowledge that states have passed legislation promoting pay transparency. As a national employer, Scorpion has made the decision to post our expected pay rate or pay range (as applicable) in all our job postings, regardless of geographic location.

  • The base salary range is $60,000 (entry-level) - $80,000 (highly experienced), exclusive of fringe benefits. If you are hired at Scorpion, your final base salary compensation will be determined based on factors such as geographic location, skills, education, and/or experience. Additionally, we believe in the importance of pay equity and consider the internal equity of our current team members as a part of any final offer. Please keep in mind that the range mentioned above is the total salary range for the role. Hiring at the maximum of the range would not be typical in order to allow for future & continued salary growth.
  • The compensation package may also include incentive compensation opportunities in the form of discretionary bonuses or commissions.

Our Benefits

We invest in our employees by offering them diverse benefits from best-in-class carriers. These benefits provide enough choice and flexibility to keep our employees and their families healthy and happy—today and tomorrow.

  • 100% employer-paid medical, dental, and vision insurance
  • Flexible paid time off, so you can rest, relax, and recharge away from work
  • Paid parental leave
  • Paid cell phone and service
  • Remote office allowance
  • Professional development and development courses
  • Regular manager check-ins to drive performance and career growth through Lattice

Work Location & Flexibility

Scorpion supports a range of work arrangements, including in-office, hybrid, and remote roles. For positions designated as remote, employees who live within commuting distance of a Scorpion office may be asked to work from the office based on team needs, collaboration opportunities, or business priorities. Specific expectations will be discussed during the interview process.

Equal Opportunity Employer

Scorpion is an equal opportunity employer and considers applicants for all positions without regard to race, color, religion or belief, sex, age, national origin, citizenship status, marital status, military/veteran status, genetic information, sexual orientation, gender identity, or physical or mental disability. We believe in creating a dynamic work environment that values diversity and inclusion.

[Reasonable Accommodations]

Applicant Privacy

When you click "Submit Application", this will send any information you add below to Scorpion. Before you do this, we think it's a good idea to read through our Privacy Policy. California residents should read our California Privacy Notice. jobs.title: Government Contracts Administrator
jobs.excerpt: ABOUT NOOKSNooks is pioneering Classified-Infrastructure-as-a-Service (CIaaS) — designing, building, and operating Sensitive Compartmented Information Facilities (SCIFs) and other secured, classified environments for the defense and national security community.
jobs.description:
ABOUT NOOKS

Nooks is pioneering Classified-Infrastructure-as-a-Service (CIaaS) — designing, building, and operating Sensitive Compartmented Information Facilities (SCIFs) and other secured, classified environments for the defense and national security community. We work with the agencies, contractors, and mission-driven organizations that keep the nation safe, delivering the physical infrastructure that makes classified work possible. We’re growing fast, operating across multiple markets, and building a company that takes both the mission and the business seriously.

About the Role

You will support the Government Delivery team by administering assigned government contracts, analyzing contract documents, negotiating routine agreements, and supporting proposal preparation. Reporting to the Senior Director of Government Delivery and working day to day with program managers and the Program Director, you exercise independent judgment on contract administration matters while acting at the direction of Government Delivery leadership. You identify contractual issues early, recommend resolutions, and guide teammates on contract administration principles and regulations. This is an individual contributor role with no direct reports.

At Nooks, we move fast. While you'll have clear ownership over your core responsibilities, startup life means priorities can shift. We're looking for a proactive problem-solver who is comfortable with ambiguity and ready to lean in wherever the team needs them most to drive us forward.

Key Responsibilities

Contract Administration

  • Administer assigned contracts from award setup and kickoff briefings through modifications and closeout, keeping files complete and audit-ready.
  • Serve as a point of contact for Contracting Officers and Contract Specialists on administrative matters for assigned contracts.
  • Coordinate between program teams and Finance on invoicing so billing matches contract terms, funding, and delivered work.

Performance and Compliance Monitoring

  • Monitor contract performance against delivery schedules, pricing, and terms, and identify when modifications, amendments, or extensions are needed.
  • Determine when customer-directed changes fall outside contract scope and raise them with Government Delivery leadership before work proceeds.
  • Track deliverables, reports, and Contract Data Requirements List (CDRL) items for assigned contracts, alerting owners and escalating risk to the Program Director.

Agreements and Subcontracts

  • Negotiate and maintain nondisclosure agreements (NDAs), teaming agreements, and subcontracts within policy and the approved fallback playbook, routing final versions for signature.
  • Flow down required Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) and Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) clauses, keeping subcontract provisions clear and compliant.
  • Monitor subcontractor performance with program managers, and investigate and recommend resolutions to claims, disputes, and complaints.

Pre-Award Support

  • Support solicitation reviews, compliance assessments, and teaming coordination in partnership with Growth.
  • Help prepare proposal contract documentation, including representations, certifications, and required forms, for leadership review and submission.
  • Draft solicitation questions and responses to customer data calls for leadership review.

The Skillset

  • Four or more years of government contracts administration experience.
  • Strong working knowledge of the FAR and DFARS.
  • Experience supporting Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) and General Services Administration (GSA) Schedule contracts.
  • Experience drafting and negotiating NDAs, teaming agreements, and subcontracts.
  • Ability to identify contract risk and develop solutions to moderate and complex contractual issues.
  • Ability to work independently while taking direction from program and department leadership.
  • Strong written and verbal communication, with advanced proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
  • Certified Federal Contracts Manager (CFCM), Certified Professional Contracts Manager (CPCM), or Federal Acquisition Certification in Contracting (FAC-C), preferred.
  • Prior experience as a federal 1102 Contract Specialist, a plus.
  • Familiarity with the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) and Contractor Performance Assessment Reporting System (CPARS), a plus.
  • Experience with Other Transaction (OT) agreements or Intelligence Community customers, a plus.
  • An active Secret clearance, preferred. An active Top Secret clearance, a plus.
  • Bachelor's degree, preferred.

Compensation & Benefits

Yearly Bonus Structure + Equity Ownership

Premium Health Coverage

401(k) Employer Contribution

Flexible Time Away

Eligibility & Clearance

Candidates must be authorized to work in the United States. An active Secret clearance is preferred. All candidates must be eligible for and committed to obtaining and maintaining a U.S. government Secret security clearance as a condition of employment.

Location-Specific Addendums

You are not attached to a single Nooks site. You support contracts across Nooks locations, working remotely with travel as needed or from the Arlington, Virginia area. Government Delivery is still setting its standards, so you will help build the tracking and file practices the team runs on.

What Success Looks Like in This Role

Every assigned contract has a complete, audit-ready file, and its deliverables, options, and modifications are tracked and acted on before they become problems. Out-of-scope customer requests are identified and raised before work proceeds. Routine NDAs and teaming agreements move to signature without leadership involvement unless a term falls outside the playbook. Proposal contract documentation reaches leadership complete and on time. Program managers, the Program Director, and Finance rely on you for accurate answers on what each assigned contract requires.

Cross-Functional Expectations

You work most closely with program managers and the Program Director, acting at their direction on assigned contracts. You support Growth on pre-award reviews and coordinate with Finance on invoicing. Externally, you handle administrative matters with government Contracting Officers, Contract Specialists, and teaming partners. You do not sign agreements or submit proposals on behalf of Nooks.

Salary Range for all departments

Salary Range
$117,000—$130,000 USD

jobs.excerpt: 🚀 Why Headout? We’re a rocketship: 9-figure revenue, record growth, and profitableWith $200M+ in revenue, guests in 700+ cities, and 18 months of profitability, Headout is the fastest-growing marketplace in the travel industry, and we’re just getting started.
jobs.description:
🚀 Why Headout?

We’re a rocketship: 9-figure revenue, record growth, and profitable

With $200M+ in revenue, guests in 700+ cities, and 18 months of profitability, Headout is the fastest-growing marketplace in the travel industry, and we’re just getting started. We've raised $60M+ from top-tier investors and are building a durable company for the long term — because that's what our mission needs and deserves. We’re growing, profitable and nowhere near done.

What we do is important

In an increasingly digital world, there is a desperate need to augment our human experience by getting us to interact with the real world around us and the people in it. At Headout, our mission is to be the easiest, fastest, and most delightful way to head out to a real-life experience — from immersive tours to museums to live events and everything in between.

Why now?

The foundation is strong. The opportunity ahead is even bigger. We’ve hit profitability, built momentum, and proven the model — but there’s so much more to build. If you’re looking to join a company where the trajectory is steep and your impact is real, this is the moment.

Our culture

Reinventing the travel industry isn't easy, but that's the fun part.
We care deeply about ownership, craft, and impact, and we’re here to do the best work of our careers. We won’t pretend like it’s for everyone but if you’re a builder who loves solving tough problems, you’ll feel right at home.

👩‍💻The role

We’re hiring a Senior Content Writer to own content quality and completeness across a portfolio within an assigned market, with a clear path toward deeper ownership of that market’s organic growth story.

This role runs on Headout’s automated content workflows. Most of your day-to-day will involve high-judgment editing of AI-generated content rather than writing from scratch. The job is not to mechanically QC drafts or rewrite everything manually. It is to apply strong editorial judgment: identify weak research, missing customer information, structural gaps, unclear claims, and content that may technically be correct but still isn’t useful enough.

As you become fluent in the system and your market, the role expands from content execution into performance analysis, opportunity identification, and portfolio-level thinking.

🤩What makes this role special?

  • High-Impact Role. You’ll own the quality and completeness of the content portfolio assigned to you within Headout’s MMP production system, while building toward broader ownership of content performance within your assigned market.

  • Hands-On Editorial Judgment. Most of your day-to-day will involve editing AI-generated product content, landing pages, and supporting pages for clarity, accuracy, structure, usefulness, and brand voice. You’ll independently verify nuanced or ambiguous claims and strengthen shallow or incomplete AI-generated research.

  • Performance & Growth Ownership. As you build fluency, typically from around month 2, you’ll start using traffic, rankings, CTR, conversion, and other available signals to understand where your portfolio is and isn’t performing. You’ll diagnose why a page or content cluster may be underperforming and identify content gaps and missed organic opportunities.

  • Play With Technology. The role runs on automated content workflows and structured tooling. You’ll develop strong fluency with the systems you work in and flag recurring friction, gaps, and opportunities to improve the workflow for the wider team.

  • Build Better Systems. The role has demanding turnaround expectations, but the workflows are designed to make that pace sustainable. We expect you to surface anything that repeatedly creates unnecessary work, weakens output, or slows execution, and help make the system better over time.

💝What skills & experience do you need?

  • You have 3–5 years of experience writing or editing digital content, with strong independent editorial judgment.

  • You Have Strong Editorial Judgment. You can distinguish between content that is merely factually correct and content that is genuinely useful, complete, and decision-oriented.

  • You’re A Strong Researcher. You have strong research instincts and are comfortable independently validating complex or ambiguous information.

  • You’re Comfortable With Systems. You’re comfortable working within structured tooling and workflows rather than defaulting to manual processes.

  • You Understand Content Performance. You have working fluency in SEO and basic content performance metrics such as traffic, rankings, CTR, and conversion.

  • You’re Analytical. You can investigate why something may be underperforming and form a reasoned hypothesis from available data and content context.

  • You’re An Owner. You take strong ownership and communicate early when scope, dependencies, or workflow issues could affect quality or turnaround.

  • You’re Comfortable With A Learning Curve. You’re motivated by becoming faster and more effective through better systems.

➕Bonus

  • You have experience mentoring or reviewing the work of junior writers.

  • You have prior ownership of a market, vertical, content portfolio, or production pipeline.

  • You have experience working with content performance data or content-led growth.

  • You have a background in travel, live entertainment, marketplaces, or e-commerce content.

  • You have experience reviewing, improving, or working with AI-generated content.

As an Enterprise Sales Executive at Toptal, you will be a key driver of growth within our AI Solutions business. In this role, you will identify, develop, and close opportunities with enterprise clients by helping them solve complex business challenges through forward-deployed AI solutions, AI software and platforms, AI services, and AI-enabled transformation.

You will develop tailored solutions that help clients move from AI strategy and experimentation into production, combining Toptal’s capabilities across AI Strategy & Transformation, Agentic Solutions, Data Services, AI Platforms, Industry Solutions, Joint Partner Solutions, and Managed Services to achieve measurable business outcomes.

Success in this role is measured by your ability to convert new enterprise relationships into durable revenue and establish Toptal as a core AI services provider embedded in your clients’ most critical initiatives.

Enterprise AI has shifted rapidly from experimentation to execution. Companies are investing in models, agents, AI platforms, data infrastructure, and AI-enabled applications, but many are struggling to translate those investments into production systems and measurable business outcomes.

The challenge is no longer simply selecting an AI model or platform. Enterprises must identify the right workflows, connect AI to their proprietary data and knowledge, integrate existing systems, build and deploy agents and applications, establish evaluation and control frameworks, drive adoption, and continuously operate and improve AI in production.

Toptal brings together world-class AI and domain talent, forward-deployed solution delivery, AI platforms and capabilities, strategic technology partners, expert-in-the-loop operations, and managed services to help enterprises move from AI promise to production.

This role exists to convert that market opportunity into new enterprise relationships and position Toptal as a strategic partner for companies deploying AI across their organizations.

This is a remote position with significant client-facing fieldwork across the US. Applicants who reside within commutable distance of a major metropolitan area are strongly preferred. You will be responsible for building a targeted portfolio of accounts via identifying, prioritizing, and developing your own book of business rather than inheriting an existing one. Once you have signed net new customers, you will partner with Client Partners to deepen and expand those strategic relationships over time.

Net new accounts may begin with a specific AI initiative, workflow, platform implementation, or business problem requiring a disciplined approach to defining the opportunity and matching the right Toptal capabilities to the client’s needs. As relationships mature, accounts become more complex, with deeper engagement across multiple business units, workflows, technology platforms, and senior executive relationships.

These accounts demand a highly consultative, strategic approach that includes navigating cross-functional priorities, understanding the client’s AI and technology environment, aligning solutions to evolving business objectives, and demonstrating credibility at the C-suite level. Success will require the ability to adapt your engagement style to the maturity and complexity of each account while consistently driving measurable client value and long-term growth.

  • Own and build a portfolio of enterprise AI accounts, with direct accountability for new logo acquisition, revenue growth, and client outcomes.
  • Prospect, pitch, negotiate, and close new opportunities in close partnership with our Sales Development Representatives (SDRs), while expanding the relationships you establish.
  • Define and execute account strategy, including opportunity creation, pipeline development, and multi-year growth planning.
  • Lead AI solution development and deal execution in partnership with AI Services leadership, Industry GMs, Practice Leaders, Pursuits, Partnerships, and Delivery teams.
  • Partner with Client Partners to drive coordinated account expansion and maximize total account value as accounts mature.
  • Shape AI solutions that apply Toptal’s capabilities across AI Strategy & Transformation, Agentic Solutions, Data Services, AI Platforms, Industry Solutions, Joint Partner Solutions, and Managed Services to clients’ most important business and operating challenges.
  • Maintain disciplined pipeline and account intelligence to support accurate forecasting and informed decision-making.
  • Lead strategic conversations with prospective and existing clients, while exercising discretion and independent judgment.

In the first week, expect to:

  • Onboard with Toptal and meet your TopPal.
  • Learn the core of Toptal’s model, our value proposition, and our deep capabilities.
  • Familiarize yourself with the tools and resources needed to be successful.
  • Dive into our sales methods, our selling processes, and playbooks.
  • Become familiar with our contracting and legal methodologies, templates, tools, and processes.

In the first month, expect to:

  • Meet key Toptal stakeholders who will support your success and the success of the overall team.
  • Learn about the Toptal AI Go-To-Market Strategy, our key sales plays, solution portfolio, partner ecosystem, and client engagement model.
  • Work with AI Services leadership to establish a portfolio strategy and build account plans.
  • Shadow key calls and client meetings.
  • Begin to meet with clients, leveraging your existing enterprise AI network and relationships, to articulate Toptal’s capabilities and identify where we can help organizations move AI into production.
  • Begin prospecting and actively engaging target accounts within your portfolio.
  • Meet with SDRs, Client Partners, and cross-functional team members to align on joint account strategies.
  • Collaborate with Pursuits and Delivery teams to understand how we design AI engagements.

In the first three months, expect to:

  • Exercise discretion and independent judgment in the negotiation of contracts, work collaboratively with clients, and help them engage with Toptal’s AI capabilities and specialists.
  • Begin shaping AI solutions that resonate with your target accounts, including forward-deployed AI solutions, Outcome Agents, agentic workflows, enterprise data and knowledge solutions, AI platforms, and managed AI services, demonstrating your comfort and ability in working with ambiguity and directly innovating alongside your clients.
  • Establish credibility with client stakeholders through informed, consultative engagement tied to their AI priorities, business workflows, existing technology investments, and desired outcomes.
  • Own your pipeline and forecast with confidence.
  • Develop proposals and close your first set of deals.
  • Actively contribute to team rituals, best practice sharing, and win/loss reviews.

In the first six months, expect to:

  • Have an initial base of active clients while continuing to build your overall portfolio.
  • Expand your buyer network and deepen executive engagement across your accounts.
  • Drive net new opportunities by introducing additional AI capabilities, platforms, solutions, partners, and managed services and displacing incumbent providers.
  • Shape and influence client priorities, aligning Toptal’s AI solutions to critical business objectives and measurable, validated outcomes.
  • Execute against a defined growth plan tied to measurable outcomes.

In the first year, expect to:

  • Have built a list of incredible client accounts, advising them on how to utilize Toptal’s AI capabilities to address their priorities and key business challenges.
  • Establish and expand a strong executive network across your portfolio, building a foundation of advocates and sponsors.
  • Begin to mentor new members of the team, teaching them about Toptal, our AI model, and how to successfully grow their territory.
  • Be recognized for your subject matter expertise in enterprise AI solutions, leveraging your existing network and relationships as well as your proven consultative selling skills to drive meaningful results for your clients and the overall AI Services team.

Qualifications and Job Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree is required.
  • 7-10+ years of experience in enterprise technology, AI software, professional services, or consulting sales, with a strong foundation in enterprise account development and complex solution selling.
  • Direct experience selling enterprise AI solutions is required, ideally including forward-deployed AI solutions, AI software or platforms, AI consulting and professional services, or managed AI services.
  • Extensive experience in consultative customer engagement and selling service-oriented, technology-enabled, or outcome-based solutions to enterprise clients.
  • Demonstrated success building a book of business from the ground up, i.e. self-sourcing, prospecting, and developing new enterprise relationships rather than relying on an inherited portfolio.
  • Proven track record managing a $5M+ annualized gross portfolio and closing $250K-$1M+ complex, multi-phase deals with enterprise clients with $2B+ in annual revenue.
  • Must be comfortable engaging C-level executives on how AI is changing their business, technology environment, operating model, workforce, and competitive landscape.
  • A well-rounded understanding of enterprise AI challenges and trends, including generative AI, agentic AI, AI applications and platforms, enterprise data and knowledge, models, workflow automation, governance, evaluation, controls, and managed AI operations.
  • Ability to have informed discussions about how AI moves from strategy and experimentation into real enterprise workflows and production environments, including the importance of context, data, integration, validation, governance, adoption, and ongoing operations.
  • Experience selling solutions involving leading AI, cloud, data, or enterprise technology platforms, and the ability to work in a platform-flexible environment across client technology ecosystems.
  • Exposure to hybrid talent models, forward-deployed delivery models, or alternative consulting delivery models.
  • Ability to build and execute account plans that lead to consistent portfolio growth and a healthy pipeline.
  • Proven success in collaborative prospecting, running virtual and on-site sales calls, and leading sales pursuits backed by a multidisciplinary team.
  • Experience negotiating complex service agreements with procurement and legal departments within enterprise accounts.
  • Ability to partner effectively across multiple internal teams to shape innovative solutions that drive client success.
  • Willingness and ability to travel to client sites, conferences, and team events (up to 25%).
  • Passion for solving client problems with creativity and urgency.
  • Regular or periodic travel to meet and engage with Toptal clients and customers both inside and outside of your geographic location.
  • Outstanding written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to work in a fast-paced, rapidly growing company and handle a wide variety of challenges, deadlines, and a diverse array of contacts.
  • You must be a world-class individual contributor to thrive at Toptal. You will not be here just to tell other people what to do.

Essential Job Functions

  • Regularly and reliably attend scheduled virtual team meetings on camera.
  • Work independently with minimal supervision.
  • Use all required digital collaboration tools.
  • Prioritize and self-manage workflows and deadlines.

US FLSA Classification: Full-Time/Exempt

This position receives a base salary and is also eligible to earn monthly commissions based on revenue generated from engagements sold. For candidates who meet the qualifications and job requirements listed above, Individual pay is determined by work location and additional factors, including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

Applications are accepted on an ongoing basis. In the US, Toptal’s benefit offerings include participation in a 401(k) retirement plan; medical, dental, and vision health insurance plans; basic life insurance coverage and short-term and long-term disability coverage; access to flexible spending, dependent care, and health savings accounts; access to telehealth virtual doctors; an employee assistance program; and flexible paid time off.
